prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: land/coastal/cryosphere products; predictable latency/documented quality; ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external processing except interfaces. Mission Control Center (Bluebell, local voice): supervision/schedules/human-authorized validated-command release/routing policy. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral, legacy logs): orbit/maneuver/access/navigation/visibility/pointing products→planning. Mission Planning System: demands/constraints/Contact booking requests→plans; Command Validation Gateway: mandatory uplink barrier. Network Control System (Lantern): authoritative circuit/routing/allocation/readiness/contact/path/maintenance status; confirms timing alarms exclude maintenance/failed-local-reference causes before forwarding→Spacecraft Operations Team (safety/authorization). Ground Network Manager (Juniper, rosters): availability/conflicts/maintenance/staffing; produces Antenna Deicing Notice; pins threatened critical paths before acquisition; latency-exceedance investigation order: carrier→routing/loss/queues/security-inspection→mission-impact declaration. Telemetry Ingest Service: spacecraft telemetry→operations/engineering/processing; receives contact-status/data-flow indicators. Orbit Determination Engine: tracking→orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report. Payload Processing Facility: calibration/processing/distribution; Primary Processing Cluster nominal; Backup Processing Cluster controlled failover/lower normal routing preference/routine firewall-return-path testing. Product Quality Service: pre-dissemination checks. Long Term Archive: authoritative data/products/records/traceability; Primary Processing Cluster transfers rate-limited during contacts, protecting telemetry/control-plane monitoring. User Services Portal: search/order/status/support. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna: primary/alternate uplink/low-rate telemetry→Mission Control Center through protected routers. Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna: high-rate downlink→Payload Processing Facility via carrier-outage-tolerant dual paths. Actors: Flight Dynamics Team—navigation/timing-quality; Payload Calibration Team—calibration/quality; Cybersecurity Desk—security/escalation, sends Security Exception Ticket for temporary baseline deviations; Local station teams—configuration/interlocks/logs; Station operators—constraints→Mission Control Center. Requirements: daily-cutoff freeze; justified contingencies; safety>timeliness>efficiency; weather governs; antenna-review corrective-actions; redundant circuits/diverse entrances; approved prefixes/authenticated neighbors/deterministic preferences/controlled dynamic adjacencies/static antenna backups; isolated administration; service-class/end-to-end latency budgets. Redundant control/dynamics reference

New part:
S078: The North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna are normally assigned for command and low-rate telemetry contacts, while the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna support high-rate telemetry reception when the visibility geometry and data volume justify their use.
S079: The Network Control System provides the Mission Control Center with antenna status, link configuration, timing references, and routing readiness before each pass begins.
S080: The Telemetry Ingest Service accepts real-time frames, validates basic framing and time continuity, and records reception metadata needed for later operational review.
S081: The Telemetry Ingest Service produces the Pass Replay Packet after a contact when the received stream must be reconstructed for engineering review.
S082: During live operations, the Spacecraft Operations Team monitors spacecraft mode, power state, thermal margins, attitude indicators, command counters, onboard storage, and fault protection messages from the Mission Control Center consoles.
S083: Console displays emphasize deviations from expected state rather than raw parameter volume, because operators must identify safety trends while a contact is still available.
S084: The console lead is responsible for declaring pass status, authorizing planned command execution through the Command Validation Gateway, and pausing the activity when telemetry does not match the expected configuration.
S085: The telemetry engineer verifies reception quality, frame loss, latency, and stream continuity, and advises the console lead when degraded link conditions could affect command confidence.
S086: The spacecraft systems engineer interprets health telemetry, confirms that subsystem states remain within flight rules, and records any anomaly context needed by subsystem specialists.
S087: The Ground Network Manager remains accountable for antenna assignment, ground link availability, and coordination with site operations when weather, equipment status, or routing issues affect a contact.
S088: The Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking measurements and validated time tags from the contact to support orbit assessment at the Flight Dynamics Facility.
S089: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine state updates and provides the basis for predicting future visibility periods, maneuver planning constraints, and antenna pointing expectations.
S090: Pass reconstruction begins when the contact closes and combines command history, received telemetry timing, ground station status, and operator log entries into a single operational narrative.
S091: The reconstructed pass record is used to confirm whether planned objectives were completed, whether any onboard event occurred outside the timeline, and whether additional engineering analysis is required.
S092: The Payload Processing Facility is also known operationally as Forgehouse in console discussions and shift logs.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
